implemented: Existing quick-switcher, mute and deafen default shortcuts now resolve through a shared typed command registry, including labels and input-focus policy.

Exact modifier matching rejects unintended Alt/Meta combinations; composing, repeated and default-prevented key events do not run commands. Physical key code takes priority, with key fallback for legacy events.

Ctrl+/ toggles a native modal shortcut help dialog from AppLayout; displayed bindings derive from the same registry used by runtime dispatch. English and Turkish labels and focused-window limitations are explicit.
Existing opt-in local/global mute and PTT collision behavior remains in place.

Mute/PTT key recorders acquire a shared transient capture lease. Overlapping recorders retain suspension until the last cleanup; local commands are suppressed and Electron mute/PTT registrations are removed while capturing. An active PTT mic is released.
Disposed native callback closures and stale asynchronous mute registration responses cannot re-enable an old binding after recorder cleanup/re-registration.

Four currently supported commands have a custom binding editor in shortcut help and desktop general settings. Device-local versioned storage validates loaded fields, rejects duplicate bindings and reserved/modifier-only chords, preserves the old state on storage failure and supports reset-to-default with conflict checks.

Runtime dispatch and help labels use effective custom bindings. Later changes to PTT/global mute physical keys take priority over conflicting command overrides. Help dialog bounds and scroll fit the viewport.

Registry now has eight commands including Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down server navigation and Alt+Up/Down channel/private-conversation navigation. Assignments and help use these actual commands. Server navigation reuses remembered single destinations; voice presentation never auto-joins or leaves calls.

Channel navigation uses the sidebar's server tree, excludes nested/archived threads and keeps DestinationView's live permission gate. Private navigation cycles group DMs and accepted DMs rather than leaking into the stale active server; pending requests are excluded.

Eight message-context commands now share the registry: edit, delete, pin, reaction, reply, forward, copy and mark unread. Focusable channel/1:1 DM Message rows run only the existing permission-filtered action registry, preserving deletion confirmation. Descendant controls/editors do not trigger row shortcuts; normal selected-text Ctrl+C is retained.

Message-context overrides permit bare supported keys without exposing global typing shortcuts. Spam-hidden, ignored-hidden and decryption-failed rows cannot invoke these content actions. Message rows have a visible keyboard focus outline.

Message S invokes explicit browser/system speech using the account rate/language without enabling automatic incoming-message reading. Explicit speech accepts up to the message limit (4000 chars); automatic incoming reading retains its 500-char limit. URL text is normalized, and unsupported/synchronously failing engines return failure to the caller.

Escape on a focused message returns focus only to an enabled composer inside the same conversation. It works without revealing hidden message content. Pointer/touch message action menus also expose speech only when readable plaintext is available.

Group spam gate now owns focused keyboard action dispatch using the same registry and capture suspension. Supported group actions are reply, existing thumbs-up reaction, owner edit/delete and scoped composer focus; hidden/undecrypted rows do not run content actions. Group pointer deletion and keyboard deletion share confirmation. Channel/DM and group deletion check account affinity after asynchronous confirmation.

Ctrl+F/P/U now dispatch search/pins/members through a typed active-conversation command event. Target includes channel kind, ID and server ID. Subscribers acknowledge only supported actions; no receiver, closed view or modal-open view is reported as unavailable rather than simulated success.

Channel commands reuse existing search, pin and member toggles including mobile member drawer behavior. DMs support pins and non-self search; group conversations focus their existing search input and toggle membership view, while unsupported group pin actions remain explicit failures.

Ctrl+E/G/S and Ctrl+Shift+U now target the active channel/1:1 DM composer for emoji/GIF/sticker/file selection. Pointer buttons and keyboard use the same picker toggles; only one picker stays open. No send permission or in-flight send prevents opening. The original file chooser, file validation, count cap, draft ownership and encryption/send pipeline are retained. Unsupported group picker commands remain unavailable, not simulated.
